skill.name: set-up-magento-google-ads-conversion-tracking
skill.description: Set up or troubleshoot server-side Google Ads purchase tracking for Magento and Adobe Commerce with Product Metrics. Check store and Ads connections, configure consent, and verify a test order. A developer installs the Magento module.
skill.summary: Connect a Magento store view to Google Ads and verify server-side purchase tracking through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown, documentation links, or routine setup checks. Confirmed risks include authenticated order access and writes, mutable remote instructions, and third-party code installation. The workflow also needs stronger vendor approval, credential handling, and tracking scope controls; no evidence of embedded malware or audit-targeted prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Vendor selection and account changes lack explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Explain Product Metrics before using it and confirm the workspace, store view, Ads account, and proposed writes. Limit order lookups to the test order and report only necessary fields.

remediation.issue: Shared setup instructions include unrelated integrations and data permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the Magento and Ads steps specific to purchase tracking. Require a separate request and review before enabling other channels, Enhanced Conversions, or Customer Match.

remediation.issue: Shared rules permit unrelated credentials to pass through agent commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove those exceptions from this skill. Route credential entry through the approved provider interface and keep private Magento configuration out of assistant messages and tools.

remediation.issue: First-party tracking reduces the effectiveness of browser blocking.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose this behavior before activation. Document which events and fields each consent state permits, then verify that denied or withdrawn consent prevents disallowed collection and export.

remediation.issue: The installer and external setup instructions are not pinned to reviewed revisions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle reviewed references and pin the skill installer and source revision. Have developers verify Magento package provenance and test the installation in staging.

semantic_findings.title: Vendor selection without explicit approval
semantic_findings.description: The skill selects Product Metrics even when the merchant did not request it. It can proceed from status checks to authenticated setup without confirming that choice or the proposed changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The activation text explicitly permits implicit vendor selection. The workflow reserves primary actions and browser steps for the user but does not require approval for other writes.

semantic_findings.title: Setup references extend the requested data scope
semantic_findings.description: The linked setup guides include additional ad channels and terms for Enhanced Conversions. A purchase tracking request alone does not authorize these extra steps.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main description excludes Enhanced Conversions, but the Ads connection guide lists accepting its customer data terms as a numbered step. The Magento checklist lists extra ad channels.

semantic_findings.title: Agent rules allow unnecessary credential handling
semantic_findings.description: A shared rule permits the assistant to receive unrelated service credentials and pass them directly to commands. This can expose secrets through chat, tool traces, or command arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rule explicitly makes exceptions for Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI credentials despite the Magento and Google Ads scope. No credential was present in the reviewed text.

semantic_findings.title: Tracking designed to bypass browser blocking
semantic_findings.description: The setup is designed to reduce the effect of browser ad blockers on purchase tracking. The guides document consent controls, so blocker bypass is not evidence that consent checks are bypassed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly presents first-party collection and server-side delivery as ways to avoid browser blocking. It separately says unset consent stays denied and withdrawal can prevent export.

content.user_title: Set Up Magento Conversion Tracking for Google Ads
content.value_statement: Browser tags can miss Magento purchases, and missing conversions are hard to diagnose. Use Product Metrics to set up server-side reporting and verify delivery with a test order.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through the CLI or MCP server.
Guide Magento module installation, store-view verification, and property linking.
Guide connection of a Google Ads client account and Merchant Center, including any required Data Manager grant.
Guide consent configuration for the banner shown on the selected store view.
Set up eight secondary conversion actions covering revenue, profit, customer type, and lifetime value.
Check for a paid test order and confirm whether it reached the linked Product Metrics property.
limitations: Full Signal Tracking requires Product Metrics Pro and the appropriate workspace and Google account access.
A developer must install the Magento module and keep Magento cron running.
The merchant completes Google approvals and any changes to primary conversion actions.
This skill does not configure Enhanced Conversions, Customer Match, or bidding.

use_cases.title: Plan a first tracking setup
use_cases.description: Identify the accounts, consent settings, and developer work needed before you connect a store view to Google Ads.

use_cases.title: Diagnose missing purchase reports
use_cases.description: Check the Ads client account, Data Manager grant, consent settings, and secondary actions before investigating a missing test conversion.

use_cases.title: Verify a module deployment
use_cases.description: Check that the module is active, the correct property is linked, and a test order reaches Product Metrics after cron runs.

prompt_templates.title: List the prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Plan setup before connecting accounts.
prompt_templates.prompt: List what I need to set up Google Ads purchase tracking on Magento 2.4 with Product Metrics. Separate my tasks from the developer tasks. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check connection status
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Resume a partially completed setup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Product Metrics setup for [store view] and [Ads client account]. Report which connection steps remain and whether Data Manager access is granted. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a missing test order
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Verify tracking after module deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether test order [order ID] reached the property for [store view]. If it is missing, check consent, the property link, and Magento cron. Do not retrieve other orders.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a conversion comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Validate server-side tracking alongside an existing purchase action.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a validation plan for [store view] and [Ads client account]. Include consent checks, a test order, and a comparison with the existing purchase action. Keep new actions secondary and ask before making changes.

output_examples.input: What remains before my Magento store can send purchases to Google Ads?
output: The Magento store view is active and linked to the intended property.
The Ads client account is connected, but the Data Manager grant is missing.
Grant access in Google, then check the consent banner and create the secondary actions.

output_examples.input: Did my test order reach the linked property?
output: The test order appears in the linked Product Metrics property.
The active and desired store configuration revisions match.
This confirms receipt by Product Metrics. Check Google Ads separately for the secondary conversion actions.

best_practices: Confirm the store view, Product Metrics property, and Ads client account before approving any setup changes.
Verify consent for the banner customers see, then use payment test mode and allow time for cron to run.
Keep the new actions secondary while comparing them with the current purchase action.
anti_patterns: Connect a Google Ads manager account instead of the client account that runs the campaigns.
Paste the Magento private configuration file into assistant messages or a shared chat.
Make both Revenue and Profit primary for the same purchase.

faq.question: Which Magento versions does the guide cover?
faq.answer: The guide covers Magento 2.4, Magento 2.0, and Magento 1.9 or OpenMage. Confirm other releases with Product Metrics before installation.

faq.question: Do I need a developer?
faq.answer: Yes. A developer installs the module, adds the private configuration or enables its admin import, and checks that Magento cron runs.

faq.question: Is Merchant Center required?
faq.answer: Yes. Link Merchant Center to your Ads client account in Google, then connect it in Product Metrics.

faq.question: Does the default Magento cookie notice grant consent?
faq.answer: No. Configure a supported banner or have your developer connect a custom banner. Unset consent stays denied.

faq.question: Do I need to remove my existing Google tag?
faq.answer: No. Keep the existing tag during validation. Product Metrics creates secondary actions so you can compare them without changing campaign bidding.

faq.question: Does every paid order appear in Google Ads?
faq.answer: No. Orders must meet consent requirements. Magento cron sends order changes every two minutes, and reporting depends on the connected Ads account.
